events.event: Ahr valley flash flood (Bernd / July 2021 floods), Rhineland-Palatinate
events.deaths: 134 in the Ahr valley, out of about 190 in Germany (NHESS 2025). Of these, 14 had cognitive impairments, largely because of deaths 'in a residential home for adults with mental disabilities' (Lebenshilfe, Sinzig).
events.forecast_quality: Mixed. EFAS sent flood notifications to German authorities days ahead, and DWD warned of extreme rain. But the official gauge forecast for Altenahr 24 h before the event said 5.74 m, while the reconstructed peak was about 10.2 m, so the size of the flood was badly underestimated.

F1.evidence: Survey of 1,315 affected residents: of those who were warned, '85% did not expect very severe flooding and 46% did not know what to do' (Thieken et al., NHESS 2023).

F2.evidence: No language-mismatch finding in the inquiry or the survey literature. Warnings were in German to a mostly German-speaking population.

F3.evidence: Germany had no cell broadcast in 2021. Warnings relied on opt-in apps (NINA/KATWARN), radio and a thinned-out siren network. '35% of respondents from NW and 29% from RP did not receive any warning' (Thieken et al. 2023). Some NINA warnings arrived late. Cell broadcast launched only on 23 Feb 2023.

F4.evidence: The Ahrweiler district declared a disaster and ordered evacuation of the 50 m river corridor only around 23:00. The flood peak reached Bad Neuenahr-Ahrweiler 'between 01:00 and 02:00 LT', at night while people slept (NHESS 2025).

F5.evidence: The Rhineland-Palatinate inquiry found that despite warning data available well ahead, county and state authorities did not turn it into concrete warnings or action. Prosecutors investigated Landrat Pföhler for negligent homicide over the 23:00 disaster declaration but closed the case in April 2024. Survivors said they were not warned; the authorities said warnings had been issued.

F6.evidence: No documented warning-fatigue finding. Low risk perception came from limited flood experience (the last comparable floods were in 1804 and 1910), not from false alarms.

F7.evidence: '46% did not know what to do.' NHESS 2025 recommends that warnings 'must focus on saving human lives – i.e. those at risk must be advised to move to safe places, e.g. to the upper floors, instead of trying to save belongings'. 37% of deaths were on the ground floor.

F8.evidence: No systematic state-community distrust finding. The vulnerability found was about age and disability (the Lebenshilfe care home), not marginalised settlements.

F9.evidence: No specific evidence. EFAS notifications covered large rivers, not small tributaries like the Ahr, which points to a scale/catchment blind spot.

F10.evidence: Climate change was widely discussed, but the state inquiry kept its focus on the warning chain. No clear evidence of blame shifted to residents.

F11.evidence: EFAS 'accurately predicted the severe risk of flooding and issued a notification to the German authorities several days in advance'. The inquiry found sufficient warning data was available but was not turned into action. The caveat is that the local gauge forecasts underestimated the peak.

S1.evidence: No structured community warning intermediaries. Some neighbours and fire brigades warned door to door on an ad hoc basis. An agent-based model found that earlier warning and evacuation could have cut losses substantially.

events.inquiry: Yes. The Rhineland-Palatinate Landtag Untersuchungsausschuss held 42 hearings and published a final report of about 2,100 pages in 2024. The Koblenz prosecutor's criminal probe of the Landrat was closed in April 2024 and the dismissal upheld in Oct 2025.
events.changes_after: Nationwide cell broadcast (DE-Alert) from 23 Feb 2023. A national Warntag and siren rebuilding programme. Revised impact-oriented warnings.

events.event: Storm Daniel and the Derna dam collapses
events.deaths: At least 4,352 killed and about 8,000 missing (HRW, citing WHO/OCHA figures). Other tallies range much higher.
events.forecast_quality: Good for the storm. The Libyan National Meteorological Centre issued warnings 72 hours ahead (WMO). Dam vulnerability had been flagged in a 2022 study. The dam failure itself had no monitoring-based warning.

F1.evidence: No comprehension study found. The main failure was contradictory instructions, not misunderstanding.

F2.evidence: Warnings were in Arabic, the local language. No language finding.

F3.evidence: 'The dams had already collapsed at 2:40 and 2:50 am respectively and the communications network in Derna was disrupted' (HRW). Taalas (WMO): the meteorological 'observing network has been very much destroyed, the IT systems have been destroyed'.

F4.evidence: The Water Resources Ministry called for evacuation at 2:59 a.m., after the dams had already collapsed at 2:40 and 2:50 a.m. The collapse happened overnight.

F5.evidence: The WMO said the NMC warned 'all governmental authorities' by email and through the media 72 hours ahead. Survivors reported the only warning was 'the sound of the dams bursting' (Gulf News).

F7.evidence: The mayor ordered evacuation of named neighbourhoods on 9 Sept. The Security Directorate then imposed a 'full curfew', and at 1:12 a.m. the Water Ministry 'reassured residents under curfew that all dams in Derna had been inspected and were in good condition'. These orders contradicted each other and trapped people at home.

F8.evidence: Rival governments and political fragmentation undermined the response. Survivors protested against the authorities one week later. HRW calls for an independent international inquiry.

F10.evidence: Aguila Saleh (head of the eastern parliament) called it an 'unprecedented natural disaster' and said people should not dwell on what could or should have been done. The WMO chief replied that 'we would have avoided most of the human casualties' with a functioning met service and evacuations.

F11.evidence: The NMC warned 72 h ahead. A 2022 academic paper flagged the dams as high risk. Science Advances calls it the 'anatomy of a foreseeable disaster'.

S1.evidence: No community warning network was documented. Collapse of the state alert chain left no redundancy.

events.inquiry: The general prosecutor opened a criminal investigation on 25 Sept 2023 into 16 officials. On 28-29 July 2024 a Derna court convicted 12 dam officials and sentenced them to 9-27 years, and a retrial was later ordered (Libya Observer). No independent international inquiry has been held, despite calls from HRW and Amnesty.
events.changes_after: Dam reconstruction and a WMO-supported rebuild of Libya's met service were proposed. Little documented change to the last-mile system.

events.event: DANA flash floods, Valencia province (Horta Sud, Barranco del Poyo)
events.deaths: 229 in Valencia province, rising to 237 in some counts. 68 victims were found on ground floors of homes and 35 in car parks and basements. More than half were aged 70+.
events.forecast_quality: Good for the hazard, weak on local intensity. AEMET issued a red alert at 7:36 a.m. on 29 Oct and the Júcar Hydrographic Confederation warned at 12:07. PMC 2025 notes 'initial forecasts failed to align with the actual rate and intensity of rainfall'.

F1.evidence: 'The low perception of risk among the general population, together with the delay in the ES Alert warning, were decisive factors' (The Conversation). The alert 'contained information deemed inadequate' and caught coastal populations 'by surprise where no rain had occurred during the day'.

F2.evidence: The alert went out in Spanish and Valencian. No language finding.

F3.evidence: The cell broadcast (ES-Alert) channel worked when used. The failure was timing and content, not reach.

F4.evidence: The ES-Alert was sent 'only at 20:11 on 29 October' (PMC 2025; The Conversation gives 8:28pm), when 'the floods had already impacted over 25,000 ha and nearly 200,000 inhabitants'. The judicial report says 'most victims died before the civil protection alert reached their phones'.

F5.evidence: The regional government, the state delegation and the CHJ traded blame over who should have warned. The CECOPI coordination centre was activated only at 17:00 despite the 12:07 CHJ warning. Three parliamentary committees and a court investigation followed.

F7.evidence: The investigation examines 'claims that official alerts were late, confusing and failed to urge people to move to higher ground'. Many victims died trying to move cars from garages.

F8.evidence: No specific marginalised-settlement finding. The vulnerability was mainly age (70+).

F10.evidence: Blame was shifted between agencies (Generalitat vs CHJ/AEMET), not clearly onto residents or climate.

F11.evidence: AEMET's red alert went out at 7:36 a.m. The public phone alert came about 12.5 hours later. 'Significant delays occurred between issuing meteorological warnings and the dissemination of alerts' (PMC 2025).

S1.evidence: No community intermediary system. The University of Valencia and some councils suspended activities early on their own initiative.

events.inquiry: Yes. A judicial investigation at the Catarroja court (Judge Nuria Ruiz Tobarra) and three parliamentary committees (Valencian Corts, Congress, Senate). Regional president Carlos Mazón resigned on 3 Nov 2025.
events.changes_after: Earlier ES-Alert protocols. Spain's government pushed for workplace leave during red alerts. Calls for probabilistic flood maps, vulnerability indices and decision-support systems linking meteorology and hydrology.

events.event: Guadalupe River flash flood, Kerr County / Texas Hill Country (Camp Mystic)
events.deaths: More than 119 in Kerr County (Texas legislative committee), 135+ across Texas. 27-28 died at Camp Mystic (25 campers, 2 counselors, the co-owner).
events.forecast_quality: Watch and warnings were timely. The rainfall total was underestimated. A flood watch was issued at 1:18 p.m. on 3 July, a flash flood warning at 1:14 a.m. on 4 July, and a flash flood emergency at 4:03 a.m. ('SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!'). TDEM said the forecast 'did not predict the amount of rain that we saw', and NWS and state officials disagreed on this.

F1.evidence: No survey data on comprehension. Camp staff 'had no idea what they needed to be doing' (legislative report via NPR), which is a plan and training gap rather than confusion over alert levels.

F2.evidence: No language finding for this event.

F3.evidence: CodeRED relies on 'publicly available phone numbers and voluntary sign ups'. 'Cell service during the flooding was also spotty, especially in the county's most rural areas.' Many children at camps lacked phones. 'Kerr County does not operate weather sirens.' (TPR)

F4.evidence: The warnings came overnight (1:14 a.m. and 4:03 a.m.). Firefighters asked for a CodeRED at 4:22 a.m., but it went out at 5:01 a.m. and some residents got no alert until after 10 a.m. The river rose about 26 ft in roughly 45 minutes.

F5.evidence: The NWS said it issued watches and warnings and held briefings. The county judge said 'We have no warning system' and 'no one knew this kind of flood was coming'. Residents reported receiving alerts hours late or not at all.

F6.evidence: Commentators noted frequent Hill Country flood watches, but no documented finding of warning fatigue.

F7.evidence: The legislative report found Camp Mystic 'had no written emergency evacuation plan that met state requirements', and staff radio calls for instructions went unanswered (NPR on the June 2026 report).

F8.evidence: The affected people were mostly camps and riverside residents, not a population marginalised from the state. Distance here was geographic and technical (rural coverage).

F9.evidence: Sirens had been discussed for years after earlier floods but never funded. That fits recurrent risk not acted on, but it is not documented as a threshold rule.

F10.evidence: The county judge: 'Rest assured, no one knew this kind of flood was coming.' The state emergency chief blamed the rain forecast. The NWS disputed both.

F11.evidence: 'Warnings Gave Officials 3 Hours and 21 Minutes to Save Lives in Kerr County' between the first flash flood warning and the emergency peak (Governing). The NWS issued a flash flood emergency at 4:03 a.m.

S1.evidence: There was no river-watch or volunteer warning network. Volunteer firefighters asked for alerts, but dispatch delayed them.

events.inquiry: Yes. Texas Senate and House General Investigating Committees on the July 2025 Flooding Events were created in Oct 2025. The joint 'Report on the Camp Mystic Flood Disaster of July 4, 2025' was published in June 2026 after about 150 interviews.
events.changes_after: New state camp-safety laws were passed. Six outdoor flood sirens were installed in Kerr County before summer 2026, though their activation plan is still a 'work in progress'. A new headwaters gauge was added.

events.event: Lahaina wildfire, Maui (non-flood comparator: wind-driven fire, same warning-chain issues)
events.forecast_quality: Good. Dangerous wind conditions linked to Hurricane Dora were forecast days ahead. Investigators found 'no evidence that state leaders prepared' despite warnings about the weather well before 8 Aug.

F1.evidence: The Maui EMA administrator said the sirens are 'primarily for tsunami': 'We were afraid that people would have gone mauka and if that was the case then they would have gone into the fire.' The public had learned the siren's meaning for one hazard only.

F3.evidence: All 21 cell towers serving West Maui had 'total cell service failure'. Maui County says its phone alerts were never received because of the outages, and it sued the carriers. The outdoor sirens were not activated.

F4.evidence: The FSRI Phase Two report timeline covers 2:55 p.m. on 8 Aug to 8:30 a.m. on 9 Aug. We did not extract verbatim alert timings from the PDF.

F5.evidence: The county says it sent multiple alerts. Residents say they never received them (County v. carriers lawsuit).

F7.evidence: 'Police closed key routes out of town to protect people from downed lines, with most of the traffic being routed along the same downtown street, gridlocking the town.'

F8.evidence: Not assessed in the sources reviewed.

F10.evidence: Blame went to utilities (HECO power lines) and carriers, not to residents or climate.

F11.evidence: The weather hazard was forecast. 'Despite being warned about the dangerous weather well before Aug. 8, 2023, investigators found no evidence that state leaders prepared.'

S1.evidence: 'Police and fire crews delivered warnings door to door, but failed to sound emergency sirens.' This was ad hoc, not a standing community network.

events.inquiry: Yes. Hawaii Attorney General commissioned the Fire Safety Research Institute: Phase 1 timeline (Apr 2024), Phase 2 incident analysis (84 findings, 140 recommendations) and Phase 3 (2025). There is also an MFD/ATF cause report. The Maui EMA administrator resigned.
events.changes_after: FSRI made 140 recommendations, covering alerting among other areas. We did not verify specific adopted changes, such as the siren policy.

events.event: '7.20' Zhengzhou extreme rainstorm, Henan (metro Line 5 and Jingguang tunnel)
events.deaths: 398 dead or missing in Henan (State Council investigation), about 380 of them in Zhengzhou. 14 died on metro Line 5. The investigation found officials had concealed and under-reported deaths and missing people.
events.forecast_quality: Good warning issuance. The Zhengzhou Meteorological Service issued five red rainstorm warnings between 21:59 on 19 July and 16:01 on 20 July. The peak hourly rate (about 200 mm/h) was unprecedented.

F1.evidence: 'Although five red warning signals for rainstorms were issued, the defense guidelines have not been implemented well. On 20 July 2021, people went to work as usual' (PMC 2022). 'The warnings failed to catch the city's attention' (Sixth Tone).

F3.evidence: No evidence that warnings failed to reach phones. The failure was the institutional response.

F4.evidence: The red warnings began about 19 h before the peak (21:59 on 19 July).

F5.evidence: The State Council found officials concealed deaths and did not start Level-I response 'even after four red alerts'. This is an accountability failure, but not of the sent-vs-not-received type.

F7.evidence: There was no suspension of work or transit. Zhengzhou Metro 'began closing some station entrances at 3:40 p.m.' but ordered full suspension only at 6:10 p.m., and the system kept running after flood defences failed around 5 p.m.

F10.evidence: The State Council report attributed deaths to 'dereliction of duty' and officials' 'insufficient risk awareness', not to nature alone.

F11.evidence: Five red warnings were issued, but 'the government did not take appropriate emergency measures'. Emergency management had 'not started the I-level' response even after four red alerts.

events.inquiry: Yes. State Council investigation team report (Jan 2022). Dozens of officials were punished for dereliction of duty and for concealing deaths.
events.changes_after: Unclear. The investigation report called for correcting the mistakes, and officials were punished. We did not verify specific protocol changes (for example, linking red warnings to mandatory suspensions) against a primary source.

events.event: Heavy Rain Event of July 2018 (Western Japan: Okayama/Mabi-Kurashiki, Hiroshima, Ehime)
events.deaths: 237 dead and 8 missing, 'including many elderly' who were late to evacuate despite evacuation orders (Nippon.com).
events.forecast_quality: Good. JMA issued heavy-rain special emergency warnings. In Mabi the municipal hazard map closely matched the actual inundation, but 'hazard maps and disaster prevention activities were not linked to actual evacuation behaviour'.

F1.evidence: The five-level system of May 2019 answered 'complaints that meteorological and evacuation information was difficult to understand'. Mabi residents 'tended to evacuate based on changes in their familiar environment rather than science-based information'.

F3.evidence: Not documented as the main failure. Municipal J-Alert and area mail were in place.

F4.evidence: 'Due to the sudden rise of water levels at night, it was difficult to judge evacuation decisions' (Mabi GPS study).

F6.evidence: Normalcy bias is discussed in Japanese literature, but we did not locate a verified source for 2018.

F7.evidence: Designated shelters and evacuation orders existed. The failure was uptake.

F11.evidence: 'Although the government issued evacuation information, there were people who did not evacuate, indicating that science-based evacuation information is not properly utilized by the public.'

S1.evidence: Neighbourhood associations (jishubo) exist, but no verified 2018 source on their role.

events.inquiry: Yes. Cabinet Office working group on evacuation after the July 2018 rains, reflected in the 2019 White Paper on Disaster Management.
events.changes_after: The five-level warning system was introduced in late May 2019. In 2021 the 'evacuation advisory' and 'evacuation order' categories were merged into a single Level 4 order ('everyone evacuate').

events.event: Extremely Severe Cyclonic Storm Fani (SUCCESS comparator)
events.deaths: Several dozen in India: at least 33 by 6 May, and later reports of 42 and higher (reports vary; we did not confirm a final official figure). Compare the 1999 Odisha super cyclone, about 10,000. Fatality per million affected: 779.3 (1999) vs 3.82 (Fani).
events.forecast_quality: Excellent. The UN praised IMD's 'almost pinpoint accuracy'.

F1.evidence: No comprehension failure reported. Messages were repeated through many channels.

F2.evidence: The sources reviewed do not document the language of messages, though they were locally delivered.

F3.evidence: Multiple redundant channels: '2.6 million text messages, 43,000 volunteers, nearly 1,000 emergency workers, television commercials, coastal sirens, buses, police officers and public address systems'. 122 siren towers in six coastal districts.

F4.evidence: Warnings came days ahead. About 1.2 million people were evacuated within roughly 24-48 h before landfall.

F7.evidence: People were moved 'into nearly 4,000 shelters', so clear destinations existed.

F11.evidence: The forecast was accurate and the last mile also worked, so this does not fit 'science worked, last mile failed'.

S1.evidence: 'More than 45,000 volunteers, 2,000 emergency workers, 100,000 officials, youth clubs, and other civil society organisations' ran the evacuation. The standing Odisha State Disaster Management Authority was set up after 1999.

events.inquiry: No adversarial inquiry (success case). UN/UNDRR reviews praised the response. UNDRR flagged power and infrastructure resilience as the remaining gap.
events.changes_after: Focus moved to resilient power and telecoms infrastructure (UNDRR 'Fani's hard lesson').

events.event: Super Cyclone Amphan (SUCCESS with caveats; CPP comparator)
events.deaths: 26 in Bangladesh, with about 2.6 million affected (IFRC/ADRC). About 2.4 million people were ordered to evacuate.
events.forecast_quality: Accurate advance forecasts. The low death toll was credited to early action and evacuation.

F1.evidence: In a household survey, 'sudden change of warning signals (16.89%)' contributed to non-compliance. The numeric signal system is a known source of confusion.

F2.evidence: CPP delivers warnings in local Bangla, face to face.

F3.evidence: 96.6% of surveyed households received evacuation orders, through neighbours (61.9%), mosques (55.4%) and social media (46%).

F6.evidence: Only 42% of households evacuated. Reasons included 'previous experiences with the failure of warnings (35.16%)' and 'disbelief in the warning system (27.85%)'.

F7.evidence: Shelter barriers: overcrowding (27%), long distances (24%) and unavailability (22%), made worse by COVID-19 fears (26% of non-evacuees).

F8.evidence: 'Disbelief in the warning system (27.85%)'. Fear of burglary (42%) and inability to move livestock (48%) reflect how little shelters offered poor households.

F11.evidence: Forecast accurate and the last mile largely worked (26 deaths).

S1.evidence: 'More than 70,000 volunteers, including 55,556 CPP volunteers, were deployed'. CPP volunteers used megaphones and flags. The one survey found their role shrank because of COVID-19 lockdown.

events.inquiry: No adversarial inquiry. IFRC DREF/Emergency Appeal final report and peer-reviewed evacuation studies.
events.changes_after: National Cyclone Preparedness protocols were revised for COVID-19 and disseminated to CPP volunteers (IFRC). The CPP continues to expand, including a push for more women volunteers (PMC 2022).

events.event: Super Typhoon Haiyan (Yolanda) storm surge, Tacloban / Eastern Visayas
events.deaths: 6,201 dead, 1,785 missing and 28,626 injured (NDRRMC figures cited in the literature). A Tacloban case-control study covered 100 deaths.
events.forecast_quality: Track and intensity were forecast well, and PAGASA issued storm-surge warnings. The predicted surge for Tacloban (about 4.5 m) was below observed heights.

F1.evidence: 'The term "storm surge" was used to warn the public before Typhoon Haiyan, but many did not understand what this meant.' 55 of the Tacloban deaths studied involved people 'surprised by the magnitude of the storm'.

F2.evidence: 'It would have been better if the term used was from the local dialect and a comprehensive description of what happens was provided.' PAGASA admitted the surge 'wasn't explained in the warnings distributed to the public'.

F3.evidence: Communications collapsed after landfall. No evidence that pre-landfall warnings failed to reach people.

F4.evidence: Warnings were issued days in advance.

F7.evidence: Staying home 'despite official recommendations' was the largest mortality risk factor. Some evacuation sites were in the surge zone, but we did not verify a source for that.

F8.evidence: 19 stayed out of 'anxiety about the security of their home and belongings', 10 believed their houses were sturdy enough.

F11.evidence: Storm-surge warnings were issued but 'the message to evacuate was not understood'. Non-evacuation was 'the greatest risk factor for mortality'.

S1.evidence: None documented for the warning phase.

events.inquiry: No single public warning inquiry found. Senate hearings were held and peer-reviewed analyses published (IJDRR 2015 'Analysis of early warning systems: The case of super-typhoon Haiyan').
events.changes_after: PAGASA pairs 'storm surge' with the Filipino 'daluyong ng bagyo' and states surge heights in metres. Storm-surge hazard maps were produced (Project NOAH).

events.event: Tropical Cyclone Idai, Beira / Buzi and Pungwe floods
events.deaths: More than 600 in Mozambique. About 1,300 across south-eastern Africa (Mozambique, Malawi, Zimbabwe).
events.forecast_quality: Landfall and winds were accurate days ahead. River flooding was barely warned: 'very limited warning about the floods' (IASC Real-Time Evaluation). The Buzi rose from 4.63 m to 9.3 m between 14 and 19 March.

F1.evidence: INAM and INGC disseminated warnings by TV, radio and car megaphones, but 'uptake and understanding of needed actions to take, as well as flood forecasting were less successful'.

F2.evidence: 'Only half the population can speak Portuguese.' 41% of people in Beira relocation sites 'do not understand written Portuguese'. Sena, Ndau and Chwabo are much better understood (TWB/CLEAR Global).

F3.evidence: Beira lost power and communications at landfall. No systematic data on how far pre-landfall warnings reached.

F4.evidence: 'Sudden flooding forcing people into trees and onto rooftops' because there was 'very limited warning about the floods'.

F7.evidence: The RTE recommends the 'urgent need to develop further contingency plans with key local actors and to establish more evacuation sites in high risk areas'.

F8.evidence: Not assessed in the sources reviewed.

F11.evidence: 'The location of landfall and expected windspeeds were accurately known and agencies and communities in the storm path were on alert' (University of Reading). The failure was in flood warning and community uptake.

S1.evidence: Mozambique Red Cross volunteers were in Beira before landfall, 'disseminating early warning messages and handing out in advance emergency shelter kits'.

events.inquiry: No judicial inquiry. IASC Inter-Agency Real-Time Evaluation (final report) and the 'Learning from Cyclone Idai and Cyclone Kenneth to Strengthen Early Warning Systems in Mozambique' report.
events.changes_after: About 1,500 volunteer Local Risk Management Committees (CLGRC) became the base of early warning, with community radio and megaphones. The death toll in Mozambique for Freddy (2023) was lower than in comparable past cyclones (UNDRR).

events.event: Tropical Cyclone Freddy, Blantyre (Chilobwe/Soche mudslides) and Southern Region
events.deaths: More than 1,000 dead or missing (President's figure, April 2023). Chilobwe township had the highest toll in Blantyre.
events.forecast_quality: The cyclone and heavy rain were forecast, but mudslides were not anticipated. 'Weather forecasts focused on floods and not the movement of mud.' An official said: 'This one [mudslides] caught us unaware.'

F1.evidence: Comprehension was not separately measured in the sources reviewed.

F3.evidence: 'Warnings were sounded as the storm moved inland. But a lot of people did not get them, including... a resident of Chilobwe' (Reuters via Inquirer).

F5.evidence: Warnings were officially 'sounded', yet residents of the worst-hit township said they did not receive them.

F7.evidence: Residents 'said they were not told where to seek shelter, and so many stayed home'. The MRCS study found people failed to act 'due to resource constraints and a lack of knowledge about necessary steps'.

F8.evidence: Communities that depend entirely on government and humanitarian help 'are left in the lurch' (IJDRR 2025). The deaths were concentrated in unplanned hillside settlements such as Chilobwe.

F11.evidence: The hazard that killed most people (mudslides) was not forecast, so this is not a case of 'the science worked'.

S1.evidence: Communities with prior Anticipatory Action programming 'were nearly 20% more likely to receive, trust, and act on early warnings' (Malawi Red Cross comparative study).

events.inquiry: No judicial inquiry. Government Post-Disaster Needs Assessment (April 2023), Malawi Red Cross comparative study, and a peer-reviewed IJDRR study.
events.changes_after: Unclear. The sources recommend integrating secondary hazards (mudslides) into forecasts and scaling anticipatory action. We did not verify adopted changes.

events.event: March-May 2024 long-rains floods (Nairobi informal settlements incl. Mathare; Mai Mahiu / Old Kijabe flash flood)
events.deaths: More than 200 by 7 May 2024 (ReliefWeb MAM floods report), later reported as over 300 for the season. The Mai Mahiu flash flood on 29 April killed at least 50-61. More than 40 died in Mathare.
events.forecast_quality: Good. KMD had forecast enhanced El Niño rains since May 2023 and 'gave more than five heavy rainfall advisories between 1 March and 15 May 2024'.

F3.evidence: The Auditor-General notes KMD/WRA alerts go through the National Government Administration Officers chain, radio and SMS. Reach was not quantified.

F4.evidence: The Mathare deaths on 4 April involved people 'trapped in their houses by floods', but warning timing was not documented.

F5.evidence: Auditor-General audit: the government 'failed to act on flood early warning information issued by the Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) and the Water Resources Authority (WRA)'. The agencies issued alerts, but early action did not follow.

F7.evidence: On 30 April the government told at-risk residents to 'relocate within 48 hours or be forcefully evicted' without providing guaranteed alternative housing (HRW). The audit recommends mapping 'evacuation routes and designate evacuation centers'.

F8.evidence: The flood impact was severe in Mathare, Mukuru and Kariobangi 'due to less solid structures, congestion, and poor sanitation infrastructure'. Displaced residents 'had not received support from county or national governments'. Demolitions followed.

F9.evidence: Floods in the late-2023 short rains gave 'harsh lessons' that were not acted on. This is suggestive but not a documented threshold rule.

F10.evidence: After the floods the state demolished homes within a riparian buffer, framing riverside residents' location as the problem. Residents were told of a 30 m clearance, but bulldozers cleared up to 60 m. A High Court later ordered compensation for forced evictions.

F11.evidence: KMD advisories 'gave the government and humanitarian organisations adequate time for early actions like providing non-food items and evacuating people from informal settlements'.

S1.evidence: Community groups such as the Mathare Ecological Network were active after the floods. No documented role in warning.

events.inquiry: Performance audit by the Auditor-General (Nancy Gathungu) on flood early warning and response, tabled in Parliament. The High Court ruled on the evictions (Nov 2024).
events.changes_after: Audit recommendations: a national DRM policy and law, a framework linking early warning to early response, mapped evacuation routes and centres. Implementation is not verified.

events.event: 2022 Niger-Benue floods (Kogi, Bayelsa, Anambra, Delta etc.; Lagdo dam release from Cameroon)
events.deaths: 603 dead, 1.4 million displaced, 2,400 injured and 82,035 houses destroyed (figures reported via Tribune/Wikipedia from NEMA/Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs).
events.forecast_quality: Good. The NIHSA Annual Flood Outlook and specific alerts named at-risk states. Advance notice of the Lagdo release was given, and NIHSA warned of Kainji and Jebba spill.

F3.evidence: Kogi household survey: '68.8% of households in flood-affected communities in Kogi state had access to early warning' in 2022, so roughly 3 in 10 did not. 'Access to flood sensitization resources from responsible agencies is poor.'

F6.evidence: Annual outlooks warn hundreds of communities every year. No study found linking this to fatigue.

F7.evidence: Residents did not relocate 'due to either disregard to the inherent dangers or inability to find alternative accommodation' (Leadership via AllAfrica, 2025, describing a recurrent pattern).

F8.evidence: Authorities note many residents were 'waiting for government palliatives, which have become politicised'. This is suggestive, not a direct measure of trust.

F10.evidence: Public discourse blamed Cameroon's Lagdo dam. Dubawa notes '80 per cent of the 2022 flooding in Nigeria was due to rainfall, not the Lagdo release', and that Nigeria's own buffer dam (Dasin Hausa) 'has remained stalled for over 40 years'. The blame was external, but this is not documented as an official strategy.

F11.evidence: NIHSA 'had issued warnings regarding imminent flooding in Adamawa, Taraba, Kogi, Nasarawa, Benue, Anambra, Bayelsa, Delta, Edo, Cross River and Rivers states'.

S1.evidence: 'Household heads remain a major source of flood education' and community leaders were one warning channel. This is informal, not a structured network.

events.changes_after: The Dasin Hausa dam acceleration was announced in March 2025 (Dubawa). Annual NIHSA outlooks continue.

events.deaths: More than 1,739 dead and 33 million affected (IWA JWCC study, citing NDMA).
events.forecast_quality: Partial. Above-normal monsoon rains were forecast and NEOC advisories were issued from 15 June 2022. Local flood forecasting and warnings for hill torrents were weak.

F1.evidence: 'Scientific terms used in early warning alerts were very professional, and people who could not read or write had difficulty understanding them' (Frontiers 2023).

F2.evidence: A community elder said flood warnings need 'a plan of action that is precisely tailored to the local community needs... and this requires the use of their native language'.

F3.evidence: 'Power failures, lack of access to TV and radio, poor cellphone signals throughout natural disasters.' The IWA study identifies 'the breakdown of the heavily-relied Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM)-based dissemination'.

F4.evidence: 'The majority of communities in 15 flood-prone districts did not receive timely warnings during the major flood events of 2010 and 2022.'

F5.evidence: The NDMA issued advisories from its NEOC, but 'NDMA's alerts rarely reach communities as trusted, actionable instructions'.

F6.evidence: Communities 'had questions about the warning's legitimacy'. Past false alarms were not explicitly documented.

F7.evidence: Communities lacked 'protected shelters to react to the alerts'. Gender norms 'restrict women's mobility, making it difficult for them to evacuate'.

F8.evidence: 'Poor socioeconomic situations, long-standing cultural norms, and low faith in government institutions' were barriers. 'Even when a neighborhood receives an alert, the majority failed to take it seriously since they... had questions about the warning's legitimacy.'

F10.evidence: The government strongly framed the floods as climate injustice internationally. We found no source that analyses this as displacing warning-chain accountability.

F11.evidence: Advisories were issued, but the sources question forecast reliability: 'others received warnings that may not have been reliable or actionable'.

S1.evidence: NGO-led interventions helped by 'tailoring solutions to individual community needs... facilitating communication'. Elders recommended sirens and loudspeakers (mosques) for low-income communities.

events.inquiry: No public inquiry into warnings found. A Post-Disaster Needs Assessment was carried out by the Government of Pakistan with the WB, ADB, EU and UNDP.
events.changes_after: NDMA upgraded the NEOC with digital/AI early warning (2023). Commitments were made under the UN Early Warnings for All initiative.

events.event: August 2018 Kerala floods (monsoon plus reservoir releases: Idukki, Idamalayar, Pampa, Banasura Sagar)
events.forecast_quality: Poor. An IISc study found 'there were no rain warnings or warnings about the amount of water reaching the dams', and 'no data available with the government over the rain received or the quantum of the water received by dams'.

F3.evidence: Banasura Sagar gates were opened 'without the public being served with no warning, customarily through loudspeaker announcements, or bulletins on radio or television' (The Week).

F4.evidence: 'Pathanamthitta was not under red alert even on August 14 night and by the next day morning the arterial Pampa had swelled.' Residents near Mullaperiyar complained of releases 'during nights'.

F5.evidence: Dam authorities 'didn't inform even the local village officer or the district collector'. The opposition alleged dams were opened without warning, and the government announced an investigation.

F10.evidence: The state framed the disaster as a once-in-a-century deluge, while critics blamed dam operations. We did not source this pairing directly.

F11.evidence: The forecast and hydrological information were themselves inadequate, according to IISc.

S1.evidence: For rescue rather than warning: 'Fishermen in 669 mechanised country boats rescued' about 65,000 people. In Pathanamthitta, about 70% of those marooned were rescued by local fishermen.

events.inquiry: Partial. A court-appointed amicus curiae (Kerala High Court) concluded the government failed 'to properly manage the water levels in dams in 2018'. There are also the CWC study report and the IISc study.
events.changes_after: A rule curve for each dam with blue/orange/red alert timings. Government permission needed '36 hours before opening the dams', with residents alerted '24 hours ahead' by loudspeaker. 24/7 district emergency centre staffing.

events.event: Rio Grande do Sul floods (Taquari valley, Porto Alegre / Guaíba)
events.deaths: 183 dead. About 422,473 displaced and 2.4 million affected across 478 municipalities.
events.forecast_quality: Good. CEMADEN 'issued moderate to very high-risk alerts days in advance', and state Civil Defence issued alerts from 22 April.

F1.evidence: 'Although the messages were clear and organized, they lacked details about impacts and specific areas, reducing the effectiveness of preventive communication and population preparedness.'

F3.evidence: 'Communication via internet and telephone services was also cut off by the floods in over 85 municipalities.' Nationwide cell broadcast ('Defesa Civil Alerta') became operational in the South only in Dec 2025.

F6.evidence: 'Alert messages inaccurately indicated flood risk in high-altitude areas far from watercourses, which created confusion and undermined the credibility of official guidance.' Over-broad warnings eroded trust (a cry-wolf mechanism).

F7.evidence: The messages 'lacked details about impacts and specific areas'.

F8.evidence: Not assessed in the sources reviewed.

F9.evidence: The Taquari valley had deadly floods in Sept and Nov 2023 before May 2024. No study found on a threshold effect.

F11.evidence: 'CEMADEN issued moderate to very high-risk alerts days in advance... However, challenges were noted in risk communication and the last-mile delivery of warnings.'

S1.evidence: Civilian boat rescues were widely reported, but we did not verify a source.

events.inquiry: No national public inquiry found. Peer-reviewed assessments cover CEMADEN's performance and the warning messages.
events.changes_after: Cell broadcast 'Defesa Civil Alerta' (Anatel with the four major operators) went into operation in the South and Southeast from 4 Dec 2025. It needs no registration and overrides silent mode. The first Porto Alegre metro alert went out on 15 Jan 2026.

events.event: Cyclone Gabrielle, Hawke's Bay (Esk Valley, Pakowhai) and Tairāwhiti; also Auckland Anniversary floods Jan 2023
events.deaths: 11 nationally in Gabrielle (widely reported; Wikipedia), 8 of them in Hawke's Bay.
events.forecast_quality: The rain was forecast but the chain was disputed. MetService wanted to upgrade to a red warning on 12 Feb but 'Hawke's Bay Regional Council was opposed', citing confidence in its flood modelling. The Government Inquiry found forecast rainfall 'significantly underestimated' actual falls.

F3.evidence: 80% of Hawke's Bay cell sites were offline. 'In Hawke's Bay, a lack of public warning systems and public notifications... significantly impacted communities' (Government Inquiry).

F4.evidence: An Emergency Mobile Alert 'was not issued for Esk Valley until 5:19am on 14 February, by which time two people had already drowned'. Some residents received it 'while on the roof or huddled in their ceiling'.

F5.evidence: 'The sense that warnings were insufficient has undermined public confidence.' People felt 'let down and abandoned'. Some 'pinned deaths on that failure'.

F8.evidence: The government report noted marae capacities and Māori expertise were 'either ignored or hampered by bureaucratic decision-making'.

F11.evidence: Meteorologists had flagged the risk: MetService 'could have upgraded weather warnings for Hawke's Bay to red the day before' but faced council opposition. The caveat is that rainfall was underestimated.

S1.evidence: Marae acted as community hubs but were sidelined officially. No documented warning role.

events.inquiry: Yes. Independent Bush Review of the Hawke's Bay CDEM response (Mar 2024: the system 'set up good people to fail'), the Government Inquiry into the Response to the North Island Severe Weather Events (Mateparae, Apr 2024), and coronial inquests (2025).
events.changes_after: Recommendations: multi-channel warning systems with manual backups for telecom outages, a review of the 111 system, and 7-14 day household provisions.

events.event: Northern Rivers / Lismore floods (Wilsons River peak 14.4 m)
events.deaths: Five in the Lismore region across the Feb and Mar 2022 events (4 in February). HRW: two women in their 80s and a man and a woman in their 50s drowned in February.
events.forecast_quality: Poor for magnitude. The inquiry found 'minimal ability to predict a flood' and recommended more investment in radar and gauges. The peak was more than 2 m above the 1954 and 1974 records.

F1.evidence: The inquiry found a 'systemic failure' in communicating risk through SES bulletins, with Lismore residents 'not understanding how severe the flooding was expected to be'.

F3.evidence: The SES 'lost up to 3,000 calls for assistance, after their overwhelmed software system turned off'. A 74-year-old: 'I only used my mobile for emergencies, and I hadn't quite known how to use it.'

F4.evidence: A hearing-impaired resident received her evacuation text 'at nearly 1 a.m.' The inquiry found 'many failures to give timely public warnings which led to the need for a high number of rescues', and said evacuation orders 'should not signal the start of rescue operations'.

F5.evidence: 'Out of 15 households interviewed, only two said that emergency services had knocked on their door and advised them to evacuate.'

F7.evidence: Door-knocks around 8:30 p.m. on 27 Feb gave 'no assistance to those unable to self-evacuate'. Destinations were not the documented gap.

F8.evidence: HRW focused on older people and people with disabilities. First Nations communities were not covered.

F11.evidence: The forecast underestimated the event ('minimal ability to predict a flood').

S1.evidence: 'Community rescues significantly outnumbered SES rescues.' 'More than 1,000 people were rescued from the floodwaters by community members' (the 'tinnie army').

events.inquiry: Yes. The NSW Independent Flood Inquiry (Fuller and O'Kane, Aug 2022; 28 recommendations accepted) and a NSW Legislative Council inquiry.
events.changes_after: Buy-back and relocation of the highest-risk Lismore residents. Resilience NSW was reshaped into Recovery NSW. SES back-office functions merged with the RFS. A single NSW disaster/warning app, a permanent State Emergency Operations Centre and more gauges and radar.

summary.notes: Nineteen events from 2013 to 2025 (18 floods/cyclones plus Lahaina 2023 as a wildfire warning-chain comparator). Two are success comparators: Odisha Fani 2019, and Bangladesh Amphan 2020, which is a qualified success. Counts are TRUE codings only. 'Unclear' means no source was found, not that the failure was absent, so F6, F8, F9 and F10 are almost certainly under-counted. They are rarely measured outside household surveys. (1) The dominant global pattern is F11+F7+F5: the hazard was forecast and warnings were issued upstream, but they never became a specific instruction (where to go, when, what to do) received by the person at risk, and afterwards agencies disputed who failed. Examples: Ahr, Derna, Valencia, Kerr County, Zhengzhou, Kenya, Nigeria, Brazil, Gabrielle. (2) Channel failure (F3) most often means the network went down during the event (Lahaina 21/21 towers, Hawke's Bay 80% of cell sites, Brazil 85 municipalities, Derna, Pakistan GSM) or depended on opt-in systems (Kerr County CodeRED, Germany NINA before cell broadcast). Several countries adopted cell broadcast or sirens only after the disaster: Germany in 2023, Brazil in Dec 2025, Kerr County sirens in 2026. (3) Timing failures (F4) cluster at night: Ahr 01:00-02:00, Derna 02:40-02:59, Kerr County 01:14-05:01, Esk Valley 05:19, Lismore about 01:00, Mabi at night. (4) Language (F2) shows up in multilingual Global South cases (Haiyan, Idai, Pakistan), which are the closest analogues to South Africa. (5) Success cases (Odisha, Bangladesh CPP, Mozambique after Idai with about 1,500 local risk committees, Malawi anticipatory-action villages 'nearly 20% more likely to receive, trust, and act') share standing, local, face-to-face intermediaries with designated shelters. Amphan also shows the limits: only 42% evacuated, with 35% citing previous warning failures and 26% COVID fears. Caveats: codings are the researcher's judgement from the cited evidence, some sources are secondary media summaries of inquiries, several PDFs (the Camp Mystic report, the FSRI Lahaina report, the MRCS Freddy study) could not be text-extracted, and their findings are taken from official summaries or press reports of them.
